phase_1.title: Phase 1 · TT-33 Trigger Release & Ignition Drive
phase_1.description: Pulling the trigger disengages the sear, freeing the spring-driven hammer or striker to impact the 7.62×25mm Tokarev primer.

phase_2.title: Phase 2 · 250 MPa Chamber Pressure Rise
phase_2.description: The propellant charge ignites inside the locked chamber, driving peak pressure to 250 MPa while sealing the cartridge case against the breech.

phase_3.title: Phase 3 · 116 mm Barrel Engraving & Acceleration
phase_3.description: The projectile engages the 4-groove bore and accelerates to 445 m/s (545 J).

phase_4.title: Phase 4 · Barrel Tilt Unlock & Operating Impulse
phase_4.description: Once chamber pressure decays safely, barrel and slide recoil locked together before the lower cam lug tilts the breech downward to unlock.

phase_5.title: Phase 5 · Spent Case Extraction & Ejection
phase_5.description: The extractor pulls the fired brass clear of the chamber and pivots it out the ejection port while the recoil spring compresses.

phase_6.title: Phase 6 · Next-Round Stripping & Breech Lockup
phase_6.description: Driven forward by the recoil spring, the breech strips the next round from the 8-round supply and locks solidly into battery.

phase_7.title: Phase 7 · Disconnector Handoff & Sear Reset
phase_7.description: Releasing the trigger hands control cleanly back to the primary sear, leaving the TT-33 staged for its 55 RPM (single-action semi-auto) cadence.

zh.headline: 苏联托卡列夫 TT-33 军用手枪：1933 年机械传奇与工程剖析
zh.deck: 费奥多尔·托卡列夫设计的苏联 TT-33 对勃朗宁 M1911 进行了大刀阔斧的战时极简重构：击锤、阻铁与供弹唇集成在一个可徒手整体拔出的模块化火控框架中，枪管闭锁筋改用车床 360° 整圈切削，成为红军征战卫国战争的钢铁利刃。 本馆以 1:1 真实工程比例重现其 20 大核心构件与完整工作循环。

acts.title: 时代召唤与研发立项：TT-33 的诞生背景
paragraphs: 1933 年问世的 苏联托卡列夫 TT-33 军用手枪 由苏联图拉兵工厂（TOZ）主导研制，定位为经典的模块化击锤组件短后坐手枪。1933 至 1954 年间苏联本国生产约 174 万支 TT-33，其结构更被中国 54 式、波兰及南斯拉夫等国广泛仿制，总产量超过数百万支。
费奥多尔·托卡列夫设计的苏联 TT-33 对勃朗宁 M1911 进行了大刀阔斧的战时极简重构：击锤、阻铁与供弹唇集成在一个可徒手整体拔出的模块化火控框架中，枪管闭锁筋改用车床 360° 整圈切削，成为红军征战卫国战争的钢铁利刃。 整件装备总长 195 mm（7.68 in）、空重 0.854 kg，成为同期手枪左轮领域最具辨识度的里程碑之一。
acts.audioScript: 第一幕，时代起源。1933 年，苏联图拉兵工厂（TOZ）推出了划时代的苏联托卡列夫 TT-33 军用手枪。1933 至 1954 年间苏联本国生产约 174 万支 TT-33，其结构更被中国 54 式、波兰及南斯拉夫等国广泛仿制，总产量超过数百万支。 它的核心设计聚焦于独创整体可拆式击发/阻铁/供弹唇模块，野战清污与维修几秒即可完成，奠定了其在手枪左轮发展史中的经典地位。
acts.focusPartLabel: 精密铣削往复式钢制套筒

acts.title: 核心机械构造与闭锁奥秘
paragraphs: 苏联托卡列夫 TT-33 军用手枪 的机械灵魂在于其「勃朗宁单铰链短后坐 · 360° 全周闭锁环 · 可整体抽出击发模块」结构体系。在发射工作循环中，枪管与套筒短距共同后坐后由下凸耳引导枪管尾端下倾脱离闭锁槽，将高压能量精确约束于承力框架之内。
制造工艺方面，关键承力件采用高温发蓝锻造合金钢精加工而成。枪管闭锁筋采用 360° 全周车床加工，极大提升战时军工量产效率，在严苛实战条件下依然保持顺畅节拍与长期尺寸稳定性。
acts.audioScript: 第二幕，核心机械原理。苏联托卡列夫 TT-33 军用手枪 采用勃朗宁单铰链短后坐 · 360° 全周闭锁环 · 可整体抽出击发模块。在每个击发周期中，枪管与套筒短距共同后坐后由下凸耳引导枪管尾端下倾脱离闭锁槽。借助高温发蓝锻造合金钢工艺与高强度配合，实现了枪管闭锁筋采用 360° 全周车床加工，极大提升战时军工量产效率。
acts.focusPartLabel: 高强度闭锁枪机头与抽壳钩

acts.title: 弹道性能、内膛工艺与实战效能
paragraphs: 该平台配用 7.62×25mm Tokarev 弹药规格与 116 mm（4.57 in 4 条右旋膛线 · 1:240 mm · 360° 全周闭锁筋），最高工作膛压约 250 MPa，可赋予弹头 445 m/s 的出膛初速与 545 J 动能，有效作用距离达 50 米。
内膛技术特点方面，116 mm 4 条右旋膛线，外周车削 360° 整圈闭锁环大幅简化战时批量车床加工。同时，发射 7.62×25mm 高初速瓶口弹，445 m/s 初速与穿透力傲视同期手枪，令其在 55 发/分（单动半自动） 的节奏下兼具精准控制与可靠输出。
acts.audioScript: 第三幕，弹道与实战表现。配备 116 毫米身管与 7.62×25mm Tokarev 口径，苏联托卡列夫 TT-33 军用手枪 实现了每秒 445 米的初速与 50 米有效射程。116 mm 4 条右旋膛线，外周车削 360° 整圈闭锁环大幅简化战时批量车床加工，展现了卓越的工程平衡。

acts.title: 人机工效、供弹哲学与百年遗产
paragraphs: 围绕 8 发容量的8 发可拆式双排弹匣壳体与 31 mm 膛轴设计，苏联托卡列夫 TT-33 军用手枪 将单发后坐冲量控制在 3.3 N·s 水平。取消独立握把与手动保险，仅凭半待击卡槽实现极简耐寒可靠携行。
如今在数字兵器库 3D 百年展厅（BAY-87）中，您可以随时通过三轴剖视、100% 爆炸视图与实时运动学滑块，零距离拆解这座跨越时代的机械工程杰作。
acts.audioScript: 第四幕，百年遗产。凭借 8 发容量的8 发可拆式双排弹匣壳体与出色的整体工效，取消独立握把与手动保险，仅凭半待击卡槽实现极简耐寒可靠携行。欢迎在 BAY-87 展位亲手切开剖面、逐件拆解，感受 苏联托卡列夫 TT-33 军用手枪 的机械魅力。

en.headline: Soviet Tokarev TT-33 Pistol: The 1933 Mechanical Legend
en.deck: Fedor Tokarev radically simplified the Browning M1911 blueprint for Red Army mass production: the TT-33 packages its hammer, sear, and magazine feed lips into a single drop-in steel module while turning 360-degree locking ribs onto the barrel for ultra-fast lathe machining. Preserved in 1:1 interactive 3D CAD scale across all 20 functional assemblies in BAY-87.

acts.title: Origins & Operational Mandate of the TT-33
paragraphs: Introduced in 1933 by Tula Arms Plant (TOZ) in Soviet Union, the Soviet Tokarev TT-33 Pistol emerged as a defining Modular-Hammer Short-Recoil Pistol. With 1.74 million built in the USSR and millions more produced as the Chinese Type 54 and Eastern Bloc variants, the TT-33 became one of the most prolific service pistols ever made.

Fedor Tokarev radically simplified the Browning M1911 blueprint for Red Army mass production: the TT-33 packages its hammer, sear, and magazine feed lips into a single drop-in steel module while turning 360-degree locking ribs onto the barrel for ultra-fast lathe machining. Measuring 195 mm (7.68 in) at an unloaded weight of 0.854 kg, it reshaped expectations across the Handgun class.
acts.audioScript: Act One: Historical Origins. In 1933, Tula Arms Plant (TOZ) of Soviet Union introduced the Soviet Tokarev TT-33 Pistol. With 1.74 million built in the USSR and millions more produced as the Chinese Type 54 and Eastern Bloc variants, the TT-33 became one of the most prolific service pistols ever made. Anchored by its hallmark design trait — Drop-in modular hammer/sear/feed-lip pack slides straight out for rapid field maintenance — it quickly established an enduring engineering benchmark.

acts.title: Core Operating Architecture & Lockup Mechanics
paragraphs: At the mechanical heart of the Soviet Tokarev TT-33 Pistol sits its Browning Swinging-Link Short Recoil · 360° Barrel Locking Ribs · Drop-In Hammer Pack. Throughout every firing cycle, barrel and slide recoil locked together before the lower cam lug tilts the breech downward to unlock, containing 250 MPa of operating pressure safely.

Constructed in hot-salt blued forged alloy steel, the assembly achieves durable field tolerances. Notably, Lathe-turned 360-degree barrel locking ribs accelerated wartime Soviet production, sustaining dependable operation under severe environmental stress.
acts.audioScript: Act Two: Core Mechanical Architecture. The Soviet Tokarev TT-33 Pistol relies on Browning Swinging-Link Short Recoil · 360° Barrel Locking Ribs · Drop-In Hammer Pack. During each cycle, barrel and slide recoil locked together before the lower cam lug tilts the breech downward to unlock. Machined from hot-salt blued forged alloy steel, it delivers standout engineering reliability: Lathe-turned 360-degree barrel locking ribs accelerated wartime Soviet production.

acts.title: Ballistic Performance, Bore Craft & Range Reach
paragraphs: Chambered for 7.62×25mm Tokarev with 116 mm (4.57 in 4-Groove RH · 1:240 mm · 360° Locking Ribs), the Soviet Tokarev TT-33 Pistol develops 445 m/s muzzle velocity and 545 J of kinetic energy for effective engagement out to 50 meters.

Internally, 116 mm 4-groove RH barrel with 360-degree lathe-turned locking rings simplifying mass production. Combined with its 55 RPM (single-action semi-auto) tempo, High-velocity 7.62×25mm bottleneck round delivers 445 m/s flat-shooting penetration, delivering disciplined accuracy across demanding field conditions.
acts.audioScript: Act Three: Ballistic Performance. Driving 7.62×25mm Tokarev through its 116 millimeter bore, the Soviet Tokarev TT-33 Pistol achieves 445 meters per second and 50 meters of effective reach. 116 mm 4-groove RH barrel with 360-degree lathe-turned locking rings simplifying mass production.

acts.title: Feed Philosophy, Ergonomics & Centennial Legacy
paragraphs: Fed by a 8-round 8-round detachable magazine body with a 31 mm bore-axis height, the platform manages 3.3 N-s of recoil impulse cleanly. Eliminates manual and grip safeties in favor of a rugged half-cock hammer notch.
Now archived in Digital Armory 3D Centennial Gallery (BAY-87), all 20 interactive assemblies can be sectioned live along three axes, exploded to 100%, and inspected part by part.
acts.audioScript: Act Four: Engineering Legacy. Pairing its 8-round 8-round detachable magazine body with disciplined recoil geometry, Eliminates manual and grip safeties in favor of a rugged half-cock hammer notch. Explore BAY-87 in live section cut and exploded disassembly to study every working link of the Soviet Tokarev TT-33 Pistol.
